translations.text: Jesus went away across the sea of Galilee, and so on.
Then the Saviour went up onto a hill and sat there with his disciples, and the holy Eastertide was then very near.
When he asked Philip where they could buy bread for the people, he revealed Philip's ignorance.
The Saviour saw the hungry people, and he mercifully fed them, both through his goodness and through his might.
The power was then in Christ's hands, and the five loaves were as if they were seed, not sown in the earth, but multiplied by him who made the earth.
This miracle is very great, and deep in its meanings. Often someone sees fair letters written, and then he praises the writer and the letters, and does not know what they mean.
He who has knowledge of the letters praises their fairness, and reads the letters, and understands what they mean. We look at a picture in one way, and at letters in another way.
Nothing more is needed for a picture than that you see it and praise it; it is not enough that you look at letters, unless you also read them and understand the meaning.
So it is also with the miracle that God worked with the five loaves: it is not enough that we wonder at the sign, or praise God for it, unless we also understand the spiritual meaning.

We cannot now expound all the five books, but we tell you that God himself composed them, and Moses wrote them, for the guidance and teaching of the old people of Israel, and also for us in a spiritual sense.
Those books were written about Christ, but the spiritual meaning was hidden from the people until Christ himself came to men and opened the secret of the books according to the spiritual sense.
As he broke the loaves, they were multiplied and grew in his hands;
The two fishes signified the psalm-singing and the sayings of the prophets. One of them made known and proclaimed Christ's coming with psalm-singing, and the other with prophecy.
The people who were fed there sat up on the grass.
But if a woman is made manly, and strong for God's will, she is then counted among the men who sit at God's table.
"The Saviour then commanded them to gather up the leftovers, so that they should not be lost; and they filled twelve baskets with the fragments."
The leftovers of the meal, that is, the depths of the teaching which worldly men cannot understand, the teachers must gather up so that they are not lost, and keep them in their vessels,
They spoke truly, in some respects: he was a prophet, because he knew all things to come, and also prophesied many things which will be fulfilled without doubt.
and we are therefore counted better, just as the Saviour said of us in another place, "Blessed are those who do not see me, and yet believe in me, and glorify my wonders."
The people then said of Christ that he was a true prophet.
We now say, with full faith, that Christ is a true prophet, and the Prophet of all prophets, and that he is truly the Son of Almighty God,
